message.content:
A CPU (Central Processing Unit) and a GPU (Graphics Processing Unit) are both processors, but they’re designed for different workloads:

| Feature | CPU | GPU |
|---------|-----|-----|
| **Primary purpose** | General‑purpose computing – handles everything from OS tasks to complex logic. | Parallel graphics rendering – excels at performing the same operation on many data points simultaneously. |
| **Core count** | Few (typically 2–32 cores). Each core is powerful and can handle complex branching. | Hundreds to thousands of simpler cores. Each core does a small amount of work but many can run in parallel. |
| **Execution model** | Serial or few‑threaded; each core can execute a wide variety of instructions. | SIMD (Single Instruction, Multiple Data) – the same instruction runs on many data elements at once. |
| **Clock speed** | High clock speeds (3–5 GHz) because each core does heavy work. | Lower clock speeds (1–1.5 GHz) because many cores share the workload. |
| **Cache & memory** | Large L1/L2/L3 caches per core; memory hierarchy optimized for random access patterns. | Smaller per‑core cache; memory bandwidth is critical, so GPUs have huge memory buses (e.g., 256‑bit or more). |
| **Typical workloads** | Branch‑heavy tasks, single‑thread performance, I/O, OS kernel, database queries, web servers. | Highly parallel tasks: image/video processing, scientific simulations, machine‑learning inference/training, cryptocurrency mining. |
| **Programming model** | Traditional CPU programming (C/C++, Java, etc.) with a few threads. | Requires parallel programming frameworks (CUDA, OpenCL, Vulkan, DirectX 12, Metal). |
| **Energy efficiency** | Optimized for low latency per operation; power scales with core count. | Optimized for throughput; many cores can be idle when not needed, but overall power can be high during heavy workloads. |

In short, a CPU is great for diverse, sequential tasks that need fast decision making, while a GPU shines when you can break a problem into many identical, independent operations that can run in parallel.
